history.dynasty: Kalachuri (12th century) per historical evidence (verify); later renovations by the Bhonsle kings of Nagpur and Maharani Ahilya Bai Holkar
history.summary: The sacred origin point of the Narmada, one of India's seven holy rivers, on Mount Mekal in the Maikal range. Legend holds that the river emerged from the matted locks of Lord Shiva (accounts vary: matted locks, throat, or foot). The heart of the complex is the Narmada Kund, the source spring from which the river begins its ~1,312 km journey to the Gulf of Khambhat; the kund is described as having eleven corners and being about 500 ft long (verify). Around it cluster some 16-24 stone temples dedicated to Shiva, Kartikeya, Rama-Janaki, Annapurna, Durga, Surya (Shri Suryanarayan), Radha-Krishna, the Eleven Rudras and others. The main Narmada Mandir is built largely of white marble and houses a black stone image of the river goddess with striking silver eyes. Narmada is also called Mekalsuta from her Mount Mekal origin, and Amarkantak is revered as Tirtharaj. Precise origins of the first structure are debated.

name: Narmada Udgam Temple (Narmadakund)
town_description: Amarkantak is a pilgrim town in Anuppur district, Madhya Pradesh, on the Maikal hills at about 1,048 metres elevation. Revered as Tirtharaj, it is the source not only of the Narmada but also of the Sone and Johila rivers, and a traditional meeting point of the Vindhya and Satpura ranges. Dense sal forests surround the temple town.

travel.road: Connected by road from Shahdol, Jabalpur and Bilaspur (verify); the temple complex is in the heart of Amarkantak town
